rationale: The parties have moved from abstract claims to quantified scenarios, but the core conflict remains unresolved: labor and Lower Saxony still reject closures and compulsory redundancies, while management, owners, and investors still insist on a materially large savings reset that may require them. The exchange is now repeating around the same thresholds and burden-sharing tests, so an external intervention to force a narrower set of decision variables is more appropriate than more open-ended rounds.
